title: Fix backend canister ID misconfiguration and enable static cPanel hosting build

requirements.text: Add a runtime-config fallback for the backend canister ID so the app can be hosted as a static site (e.g., on cPanel) without requiring build-time injection, while preserving the existing current behavior when VITE_BACKEND_CANISTER_ID is correctly set at build time.

quotes: yes i wanna host the website in my cPanel on my domain
The backend canister ID is not configured. The deployment must inject this value before the application can connect to the backend service.

acceptanceCriteria: If VITE_BACKEND_CANISTER_ID is set at build time, the app uses it exactly as before and no new configuration file is required.
If VITE_BACKEND_CANISTER_ID is missing/empty at build time, the app can still be configured by editing a static file in the deployed site (no rebuild required) and then reloading the page.

Backend connectivity diagnostics (the existing error screen) correctly reflects whether the backend canister ID came from build-time env or runtime config, and shows the configured principal once set.
No changes are made to immutable frontend paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.

requirements.text: Create a cPanel-friendly static deployment bundle and documentation: ensure the production build output includes an index.html entry point and all required assets, and add clear steps for uploading to cPanel including SPA routing configuration (refreshing deep links like /dashboard should work).

quotes: make it so i can download the code and host the website myself so make sure there a index.html
yes i wanna host the website in my cPanel on my domain

acceptanceCriteria: The build output folder (dist) contains index.html and the referenced JS/CSS/assets produced by the build.
Documentation is added/updated with cPanel upload steps and an example Apache .htaccess rewrite rule so direct navigation/refresh on app routes works (SPA fallback to /index.html).
Documentation includes instructions for setting the backend canister principal for self-hosting (using the runtime-config mechanism from REQ-1).

requirements.text: Fix the dashboard/admin-dashboard flows so authenticated users can reach the dashboard via the Get Started flow and place orders without being blocked by configuration errors when properly configured; keep the current design and behavior unchanged except for error fixes.

quotes: fix the ordering placing errors just come up when trying to use dashboard (get started button) admin dashboard fix them.
2.should I keep its current design and behavior and only fix errors

acceptanceCriteria: With a valid backend canister ID configured, an authenticated user can load the dashboard without seeing the configuration error screen.
With a valid backend canister ID configured, a user can complete the checkout flow that creates orders (Cart -> create orders -> redirected to /dashboard with success modal).
Admin dashboard routes continue to be protected (admin-only) and load without runtime exceptions when backend configuration is valid.
When backend configuration is missing/invalid, the UI continues to show a clear configuration error state (no infinite spinners or silent failures).

requirements.text: Improve the deployment scripts/docs so that when deploying to the Internet Computer, the build reliably injects VITE_BACKEND_CANISTER_ID (retrieving it via dfx when available), and the failure mode is actionable; do not hardcode canister IDs into version control.

quotes: look if it has one then dont setup just fix if not set one up

acceptanceCriteria: Mainnet/IC deployment flow continues to validate a missing/invalid backend canister ID and explains how to obtain it via dfx.
No canister principal IDs are committed into .env.production or other tracked env files.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo (no multi-canister backend architecture).
Do not edit files under frontend/immutablePaths (compose them instead).
Use English for any user-facing text.
nonGoals: Redesigning the dashboard/admin dashboard UI or changing existing user-facing behavior beyond fixing errors and enabling configuration.
Adding third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is supported).
Adding external databases or non-Motoko backend services.
